The first cheek: fast media downloads in one small Rust binary.

- Parallel byte ranges over separate connections (8 by default, `-N`), with chunk sizes that keep every connection busy to the end
- Parallel HLS segments, written in order; init segments supported
- Resumable: `.part` files plus a `.cheek` note of finished chunks; Ctrl+C and run again
- Reads yt-dlp's JSON (`yt-dlp -J … | cheek --info-json -`) or calls yt-dlp itself for the 1,800 sites it knows
- Own extractor for direct files, HLS playlists and pages with `og:video`, `<video>` or JSON-LD
- ffmpeg merge without re-encoding, audio extraction (`-x`), yt-dlp's output templates
- `--json` progress events for apps; used by [Hamstr](https://github.com/Mailo037/Hamstr) on Android

Measured: 1.7x faster than yt-dlp on archive.org, 1.2x on a direct 1.1 GiB file, and the same speed on YouTube, where a single connection already fills the line. See the README for the details.

Binaries: Linux (static musl, x86_64 and aarch64), Windows x86_64, macOS (Apple silicon and Intel), and Android (arm64-v8a, armeabi-v7a, x86_64) for apps.
